hints: Notice the diagram marks $53^{\circ}$ between the diffracted ray to the fourth order maximum and the centre line - this is the diffraction angle $\theta$.
Recall the grating condition for normal incidence is $d \sin \theta = n \lambda$ with line spacing $d = 2.7 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$ and order $n = 4$.
Rearrange to $\lambda = d \sin 53^{\circ} / 4$ and check the result is in metres and in the visible range around $10^{-7} \text{ m}$.
walkthrough: Identify the given values from the question: order $n = 4$, angle $\theta = 53^{\circ}$ from the centre line, and grating spacing $d = 2.7 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$.
State the governing rule for intensity maxima at normal incidence: $d \sin \theta = n \lambda$, where $\lambda$ is the wavelength.

Calculate the intermediate path difference: $(2.7 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}) \times 0.799 \approx 2.16 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$, then divide by 4 to get $\lambda \approx 5.4 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.
Check units and sense: the result is in metres and lies in visible light, while omitting $n$ or using $\cos \theta$ gives the other listed values. This is option B.

options.A: This uses $\cos 53^{\circ}$ instead of $\sin 53^{\circ}$ with $n = 4$, giving about $4.1 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.
options.B: This correctly uses $\lambda = d \sin \theta / n$ with $d = 2.7 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$, $\theta = 53^{\circ}$ and $n = 4$.
options.C: This uses $\cos 53^{\circ}$ instead of $\sin 53^{\circ}$ and omits the fourth order by using $n = 1$.
options.D: This omits division by the order and calculates $d \sin 53^{\circ}$, which is the path difference for $n = 1$.
